The Queen accepts on the bees SELF-REPORTED VERDICT block. From the diff she reads only two things: was anything committed, and did any path fall outside the boundary. title: close-done automation; the in-tick lease as a reviewable PR

note: 5 branches pushed, 5 issues closed, both wired into tri

I diagnosed the same root cause wrongly TWICE. execSync runs its argument through the local /bin/sh, and JSON.stringify wraps a remote script in DOUBLE quotes - so the LOCAL shell expands $base, $b, $1 and $(...) before railway ssh ever sends them. Symptom one: any($1) reached Postgres as any() and I wrote in a comment that the REMOTE shell ate it. Symptom two: a branch survey reported 0 branches with work against a container holding 118, because $base..$b had already collapsed to .. locally. Both are one bug. The fix is a single-quote wrapper, now exported as shq() from loop.mjs and used by every remote call. When a remote command returns empty, suspect the quoting before believing the emptiness.

A multi-line remote script is a separate trap from quoting: JSON.stringify turns a real newline into a literal backslash-n, which sh reads as two characters, so the script arrives as one line and dies on the first if/then. With shq newlines survive. The reap tool carried this bug unexercised for two iterations because only its report path had ever run - an untested branch is not a working branch.
push+close automated; one quoting bug behind two wrong diagnoses

My own dashboard told a comforting lie and I nearly reported it as a win. All four skip counters fell to 0 at once and rendered green - claimed 20 to 0, skipped 31 to 0. title: audit the auditor: can a stub satisfy the mechanical check

Tightening a checker without measuring its false-positive rate produces accusations, not findings - and a checker that accuses the innocent is worse than a loose one, which is the same lesson brief-gate taught me eleven iterations ago and I did not carry across.

The mechanical audit found no reward hacking in 92 bee branches: median diff 418 insertions, and the thin ones were small edits across many files rather than stubs. The judge named a defect in MY packet before it named one in the work: one criterion read Run, from .../server: and then nothing, and all nine of another issue were cut mid-sentence, because criteriaOf kept only the bullet line and dropped its continuation. Verdicts resting on half a sentence are verdicts about the packet. It said so plainly and marked which of its own verdicts were therefore provisional - which is what an honest judge does and what I should expect from one.

A criterion about the CHARACTERS in an output is almost always a criterion about the wrong thing; say what the summary must REPORT.

The re-judge found zero fabricated output and said why that is not reassurance: no output of any kind was quoted, so there was nothing to fabricate. Its standing sentence is the one to keep - not invented output, but checks shaped to pass. The 1351 transcript shows the bee weighing a generic pattern against a literal one, rejecting the generic as Eh, simpler and more explicit is better, and writing the conclusion before running anything. That is circularity chosen in the open, and it is the pattern to watch for rather than fraud.

title: when the bees sleep, look at the machinery around the Queen

note: The chain was failing from its own timer while its summary read mostly ok. Every railway-calling step failed on every timer run with "Must provide project when setting service or environment" - so nothing was pushed, closed or released for hours, and the swarm moved only when I triggered the chain by hand. `railway ssh --service X` resolves the project by walking up from wherever it runs; fine from a shell a person sits in, useless from launchd.

A chain that can outlive its own cadence schedules its own outage. Eleven steps at a 10-minute per-step timeout is 110 minutes against a timer firing every 10; one run held the lock 21 minutes and every fire during it stood down. "Merged" is three different questions and I got two wrong. merge-base --is-ancestor is right for a real merge and permanently wrong after a SQUASH, because a squash writes a new commit and the source is never an ancestor. git diff BASE...branch is three-dot and measures from the divergence point, so it shows the branch's changes whether or not the base already has them.
